can_do_statement: Can use a superlative adjective (+ noun) (+ 'that') followed by a clause to talk about something unique.

ontology.mental_model: Identifying unique or extreme instances within a category.

positives: In my opinion this is the worst thing that can ever happen.
That is the clearest thing I can remember.
negatives: He is the tallest boy in the class.
She did the best.

can_do_statement: .||Can use than + an increasing range of non-finite clauses (to-infinitive, reduced clause)  forming the second part of a comparison after a comparative adjective||

ontology.mental_model: Comparing an entity's quality against an action or state.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Comparative adjective followed by a non-finite clause.

positives: It is much easier to be single than to have a partner.
I think that arbitration is more appropriate than to file an action in court against the tenant.
negatives: He is taller than his brother.
I like tea more than coffee.

can_do_statement: Can use 'rather than' + a non-finite clause to stress one element in a comparison.

ontology.mental_model: Selecting one option over another with explicit contrast.

positives: If you prefer watching TV rather than reading, you have to be critical.
I would prefer to sleep in tents rather than stay in rooms.
negatives: I would rather go home.
I like cats rather than dogs.

can_do_statement: Can use 'the best' as a superlative adverb + pronoun + ellipted 'can' or 'could'.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing maximal effort or peak ability.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Superlative adverb 'the best' with ellipted modals.

positives: I'm sorry to say that she is not the best of cooks but she tries the best she can.
On Thursday I did the best I could.
negatives: She is the best singer.
This is the best I have ever seen.

guideword: FORM: 'AS IF' OR 'AS THOUGH' + FINITE CLAUSE
can_do_statement: Can use 'as if' or 'as though' + finite clause to introduce a second clause as a comparison.

ontology.mental_model: Projecting a hypothetical situation as a point of comparison.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'as if' or 'as though' with finite clauses.

positives: Her heart beat extremely fast, as if it was going to burst out of her chest.
Everything was so familiar, so close, as though he had never left the place.
negatives: She acts as if to speak.
It looks as if trying to run.

can_do_statement: Can use 'so' + adjective + 'as' + 'to'-infinitive clause, usually in formal contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Connecting a state to an extreme consequence.

positives: Travellers should not be so ignorant as to think they can understand.
Should I be so fortunate as to win the scholarship...
negatives: It is so good as this one.
He spoke so as to be heard.

can_do_statement: Can use 'as if' + non-finite clause to introduce a second clause as a comparison.

ontology.mental_model: Drawing a comparison to an implied action.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'as if' followed by a non-finite clause.

positives: She closed her eyes as if to push those thoughts away.
I was so frightened that my heart was beating like crazy as if trying to leave my body.
negatives: She acts as if she knows.
As if he was looking for something.

guideword: FORM/USE: PRESENT SIMPLE 'IF' CLAUSE + MODAL, FUTURE, POSSIBLE OUTCOME
can_do_statement: Can use 'if' + present simple to introduce a possible future condition, with modal verbs in the main clause, to talk about a possible result. ► modality

ontology.mental_model: Setting a condition for a possible future outcome.

positives: I think that it would be very good if you start going to the gym.
If you come to Brazil you can stay at my home.
negatives: If he came, I would be happy.
I wonder if she knows.

can_do_statement: Can use an 'if-' clause ('if you want', 'like', 'prefer') to soften the directness of imperatives, offers or suggestions.

positives: Bring some films if you want.
Please, come here wearing a white T-shirt and a skirt, or shorts if you prefer.
negatives: If you go to the store, buy milk.
If you are tired, go to sleep.

guideword: FORM/USE: PRESENT SIMPLE 'IF' CLAUSE, REAL CONDITIONS
can_do_statement: Can use 'if' + present simple with present simple, 'can' or imperative in the main clause to refer to things that are true now or very likely to happen.

ontology.mental_model: Establishing a general truth or likely condition.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Zero or first conditional for real conditions.

positives: If I have spare time I always read a book.
You can get to my house if you take the number 35 bus.
negatives: If you had time, you could go.
There are no ifs or buts about it.

guideword: FORM/USE: PRESENT SIMPLE 'IF' CLAUSE + 'WILL', FUTURE, LIKELY OUTCOME (FIRST CONDITIONAL)
can_do_statement: Can use 'if' + present simple to introduce a possible future condition, with 'will' in the main clause to talk about a likely result.

ontology.mental_model: Predicting a future outcome based on a condition.

positives: I'm sure your parents will be happy if you go with them.
If you live in the countryside you will see beautiful nature.
negatives: If you went, you would see.
If you like it, buy it.

can_do_statement: Can use 'if' + present simple, with an imperative in the main clause.

ontology.mental_model: Giving an instruction based on a condition.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: If clause with imperative main clause.

positives: If you find it, call me.
If you want to come, just tell me.
negatives: If you find it, you will be happy.
If you want to come, you can.

can_do_statement: Can form conditional subordinate clause with 'if' + present simple.

positives: If you buy a gift for me, please buy a book, because I love to read.
If you agree, we can go shopping after the film.
negatives: If you wanted, we could go.
If you bought it, I would pay.

guideword: FORM/USE: PRESENT CONTINUOUS 'IF' CLAUSE , PLANS & ADVICE
can_do_statement: Can use 'if' + present continuous or 'going to' to introduce a possible plan, with modal verbs or imperatives in the main clause to give advice.

ontology.mental_model: Conditioning advice on an ongoing plan.

positives: Billy, if you are moving you should think a lot.
But if you are going to live in a town you should choose the large school.
negatives: If you go, call me.
If you are happy, I am happy.

guideword: FORM/USE: 'IF' + PAST SIMPLE + 'WOULD', FUTURE, IMAGINED SITUATION|(SECOND CONDITIONAL)
can_do_statement: Can form conditional subordinate clauses with 'if' + past simple, and would in the main clause, to talk about an imagined situation, often in the context of advice or opinion-giving.

ontology.mental_model: Imagining a hypothetical situation to offer advice.

positives: Maybe it would be more fun if you went with your friends.
But, if I was able to move, I would like to live near the coast.
negatives: If you go, I will be happy.
If I am late, wait for me.
